title: Anchored Reinitialization of Three-Cavity Filter with Layer 1-2 Constraints
scientific_hypothesis: Constraining the first two layers to remain near their iteration 18 optimal values (467.69 nm, 389.19 nm) with ±15 nm bounds will preserve the input coupling resonance condition that contributed to previous performance while allowing fine-grained optimization of the remaining 19 layers. The quadratic penalty beyond ±25 nm will dampen large-step excursions that may destabilize the cavity resonance.
design_principle: Multi-cavity Fabry-Perot bandpass filter with anchored boundary layers to maintain input coupling condition while optimizing internal cavity structure
proposed_topology: 21-layer alternating Ge/ZnS stack on CaF2 substrate, starting with Ge layer 1
design_variables: layer 1 (Ge) thickness bounded to [452.69, 482.69] nm with target 467.69 nm
layer 2 (ZnS) thickness bounded to [374.19, 404.19] nm with target 389.19 nm
quadratic penalty weight 10x for layer 1-2 deviations beyond ±25 nm from targets
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 4.15-4.35 μm and 4.55-4.75 μm passbands
minimize mean transmittance in 3.60-4.00 μm and 4.85-5.20 μm stopbands
manufacturing_considerations: all layers within 50-500 nm range for conventional deposition
Ge and ZnS are conventional IR dielectrics
theory_basis: Transfer-matrix method for planar multilayer interference
Fabry-Perot cavity resonance condition: (φ1 + φ2 − 2δ)/2 = kπ
expected_advantages: Reduces optimizer search space for boundary layers
May improve convergence stability compared to free optimization
known_risks: Anchoring may prevent discovery of better boundary layer configurations
Quadratic penalty may create local minima
21 layers may still be insufficient for dual-band requirement
execution_request_english: Optimize a 21-layer alternating Ge/ZnS dielectric stack on CaF2 substrate at normal incidence. Layer 1 (Ge) thickness bounded to [452.69, 482.69] nm with target 467.69 nm. Layer 2 (ZnS) thickness bounded to [374.19, 404.19] nm with target 389.19 nm. Layers 3-21 thickness bounded to [50, 500] nm. Apply quadratic penalty weight 10x for layer 1-2 deviations beyond ±25 nm from targets. Maximize mean transmittance in passbands [4150, 4350] nm and [4550, 4750] nm. Minimize mean transmittance in stopbands [3600, 4000] nm and [4850, 5200] nm. Use gradient-based thickness optimizer. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 3600-4000 nm, 4150-4350 nm, 4550-4750 nm, 4850-5200 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 4.15-4.35 um and 4.55-4.75 um bands; low transmittance in 3.60-4.00 um and 4.85-5.20 um bands. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high transmittance in stopbands; high reflectance in passbands. manufacturing constraints: no metal layers; maximum 24 layers; conventional depositable infrared inorganic dielectric materials.
revision_reason: Implements feedback directive for anchored reinitialization of layers 1-2 to iteration 18 optimal values with tight bounds and quadratic penalty to dampen large-step optimizer excursions
